items.title: Understanding ADLs and IADLs: The Basics of Caregiving Assessments
items.summary: If you’ve started the process of applying for Medicaid Home and Community Based Services Waivers or any other long-term care services, you’ve likely heard the terms ADLs and IADLs. These aren't just clinical jargon; they are the "measuring sticks" that state assessors use to determine exactly how much help a person needs to remain safely at home.

items.title: Structured Family Caregiving (SFC) in Ohio: A 2026 Guide for Families
items.summary: Structured Family Caregiving is a Medicaid-funded service available in 11 states across the USA, including Ohio. In Ohio specifically, SFC is administered through agency providers that participate in key state programs: the Ohio Home Care Waiver, PASSPORT, or MyCare Ohio.

items.title: Medicare vs. Medicaid: Why Your Insurance Doesn’t Pay for Long-Term Home Care
items.summary: Clearing up the "Medicare Myth" for Ohio families navigating the search for in-home support.

items.title: Can You Get Paid to Care for Your Spouse in Ohio?
items.summary: Yes, Ohio Medicaid can pay you to care for your spouse. Two conditions must be met. Here's how it works under PASSPORT, MyCare Ohio, SFC, and other waivers.

items.title: Free Farmers Market Vouchers for Ohio Seniors: Apply Before May 22, 2026
items.summary: Ohio seniors 60+ can get $50 in free vouchers for fresh produce at farmers markets through SFMNP. Enrollment is April 22 – May 22, 2026. Here's how to apply.

items.title: Facts vs Fiction: Caregiver Edition for 2026
items.summary: Deciding to become a paid caregiver for a loved one is a huge life shift. Because it sounds like a "hack," many families worry it’s too good to be true. Let’s clear the air and look at the actual facts for 2026.

items.title: My Aging Parent Can’t Live Alone Anymore: A Guide to Every Option
items.summary: It usually starts with a phone call. An unexpected fall, a trip to the ER, or a sudden realization that the status-quo is no longer safe. If you’re feeling overwhelmed, you’re not alone. Most families don't "plan" for long-term care; they react to a crisis. The good news? You have more options than just a nursing home. This guide will help you assess your parent’s current safety and navigate the different care models available.

items.title: How to Transition from Child to Caregiver
items.summary: A practical guide to transitioning from child to caregiver, with tips for difficult conversations with aging parents and Ohio caregiver support resources.

items.title: Finding Respite Care in Ohio: A Complete Guide for Family Caregivers
items.summary: Respite care services in Ohio can give family caregivers the break they need—without sacrificing safety or quality of care. This guide covers in-home respite, adult day services, and overnight options, plus how Medicaid waivers and other programs may help pay. Learn where to start, what to ask for, and how to connect with your local Area Agency on Aging.

items.title: 5 Essential Skills Every Family Caregiver Needs to Learn
items.summary: If you're caring for a parent or loved one at home, developing specific caregiving skills can make a significant difference in both safety and quality of care. These five foundational competencies keep your loved one safer, protect you from injury and burnout, and ensure you're providing the level of care they need. Whether you're exploring paid caregiving programs in Ohio or simply want to improve your caregiving approach, mastering these skills is essential.

items.title: 2026 Ohio Home Safety Checklist: Get Up to $15,000 in Waiver Support
items.summary: Whether you’re a senior living independently or a family member caring for an older loved one, creating a safe and comfortable home is one of the most important ways to protect independence and peace of mind. It’s essential to reduce fall risks and consider age‑related changes—such as vision, balance, and memory—when setting up each space. With a few thoughtful adjustments, we can make everyday life easier, safer, and more enjoyable. At CareOasis, we believe every older adult deserves the chance to age gracefully at home. A safe home is the foundation for that independence.

items.title: DODD vs Aging Waiver in Ohio: Which Program Do You Qualify For?
items.summary: Trying to get Medicaid waiver support in Ohio? The first step is figuring out which system you belong to. Ohio has two separate waiver tracks: DODD waivers for people with developmental disabilities that started before age 22, and aging waivers (like PASSPORT) for older adults or people with disabilities acquired later in life. Applying to the wrong system can cost you months of time. This guide explains the key differences, who qualifies for what, and which agency to contact first.

items.title: Ohio Medicaid Income Limits (2026): the numbers, the common sticking points, and what to do next
items.summary: Figuring out Ohio Medicaid income limits shouldn't feel like a second job—but for many families trying to access in-home care, it does. Whether you're exploring PASSPORT, MyCare Ohio, or Structured Family Caregiving, income is often the first hurdle you'll face. This guide breaks down the 2026 income limits by category, explains when assets matter (and when they don't), and walks you through what to do if you're over the limit. Includes current income charts, eligibility pathways for long-term care support, and practical next steps for Ohio families navigating Medicaid.

items.title: How to Apply for Caregiving Benefits in Ohio (PASSPORT, MyCare Ohio, and Structured Family Caregiving)
items.summary: Learn how to apply for caregiving benefits in Ohio through Medicaid programs like PASSPORT and MyCare Ohio, and discover how family caregivers can get paid for providing in‑home care.

items.title: Next Generation MyCare Ohio: What You Should Know Before the 2026 Rollout
items.summary: Starting in January 2026, the Next Generation MyCare Program will simplify healthcare for Ohioans eligible for both Medicare and Medicaid. Learn about the updates, enrollment details, program changes, and resources for caregivers.

items.title: Empowering Ohio's Seniors: Exploring the PASSPORT Waiver
items.summary: If you live in Ohio, you might have heard of the Ohio PASSPORT Waiver. PASSPORT is an acronym that stands for Preadmission Screening System Providing Options and Resources Today. It is a Medicaid Waiver that helps older Ohioans live independently in their own homes for longer by providing options for long-term care services and support.

items.title: How to Support a Family Caregiver: The Words and Actions that Truly Help
items.summary: Supporting a family caregiver goes beyond offering help; it’s about providing the right kind of help. In this blog, we explore specific actions and words that offer genuine support to those who tirelessly care for their loved ones. Learn how to make a meaningful difference in a caregiver's life with practical tips on providing specific assistance, acknowledging their efforts, being a non-judgmental listener, and more. Show caregivers they’re not alone in their journey with authentic empathy and tangible support. Read on to find out how your actions can truly help.

items.title: What is the HCBS Waiver Program?
items.summary: Discover the comprehensive range of Medicaid waiver programs available in Ohio designed to support older adults, people with disabilities, and youth with complex needs. Learn about eligibility requirements, services covered, and how these programs enable individuals to thrive in their own homes and communities. Dive into our friendly guide to find the right program for you or your loved one!

items.title: What is Care and When do you need it as a Senior Citizen?
items.summary: Navigating the world of elder care can be overwhelming, especially when trying to determine the best type of care for a senior citizen. This guide breaks down the five main types of care: at-home caregivers, senior living facilities, assisted living, nursing homes, and memory care units. Learn about the services each type provides, along with their associated costs, to make an informed decision for yourself or a loved one.

items.title: When a Client Wants to Thank Their Caregiver: A Guide to Ethical Estate Planning
items.summary: When a client wishes to leave a portion of their estate to their caregiver, ethical and legal considerations are paramount. This guide outlines the necessary steps to protect the client's wishes and avoid potential legal issues, including the importance of consulting an estate planning attorney and maintaining transparency with family and friends.
